This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at (web: `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable shot <page>`), and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (long ones as a map: read the sections your task needs), the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Some playbooks come in parts; read the part this request needs in the same step: [reference/new-work-world.md](reference/new-work-world.md) when a visual world is created or replaced (a redesign, a new look, or no established world), [reference/new-work-comp.md](reference/new-work-comp.md) for a build from an approved comp or on a comp-led build path, and [reference/critique-rubric.md](reference/critique-rubric.md) for a critique whose Assessment A runs in this context (a native platform, or no sub-agent tool); a delegated Assessment A gets the rubric's path in its prompt instead. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On the first refusal or failure, don’t retry; send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at (web: `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable shot <page>`), and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (long ones as a map: read the sections your task needs), the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface, a replacement visual world, or a build from an approved comp. Some playbooks come in parts; read the part this request needs in the same step: [reference/new-work-world.md](reference/new-work-world.md) when a visual world is created or replaced (a redesign, a new look, or no established world), [reference/new-work-comp.md](reference/new-work-comp.md) for a build from an approved comp or on a comp-led build path, and [reference/critique-rubric.md](reference/critique-rubric.md) for a critique whose Assessment A runs in this context (a native platform, or no sub-agent tool); a delegated Assessment A gets the rubric's path in its prompt instead. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

Choose the mode from the requested surface, not the product, and persist it only in that surface brief. A tool's landing page is still Persuade; a fashion house's documentation is still Read; a docs index is Read, not Persuade. See [new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for new surfaces and [operate.md](reference/operate.md) for deeper Operate/Read guidance.

*** Add File: /home/mike/nexus-wt/v130-delegation-runtime/docs/v1.3.0/BATCH.md
+# `/batch` on the operation engine
+
+`/batch` accepts the same JSON work-unit format as `nexus operation run`. It validates the whole dependency graph before starting, then stores and executes it through `OperationStore`, `ConvergenceScheduler`, and `OperationRunner`.
+
+```json
+{
+  "id": "docs-and-tests",
+  "objective": "Update the guide and verify the examples",
+  "units": [
+    {
+      "id": "guide",
+      "title": "Update the guide",
+      "role": "implementer",
+      "prompt": "Update the guide examples for the new API",
+      "authorizedScope": ["docs/guide.md"]
+    },
+    {
+      "id": "verify",
+      "title": "Verify the examples",
+      "role": "tester",
+      "prompt": "Run the documented examples and report the results",
+      "dependsOn": ["guide"]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+The accepted fields are the operation fields: `objective`, optional `id`, `units`, optional `resources`, `discoverCatalog`, `policy`, `git`, and `boundaries`. A unit uses `prompt` for its task, optional `role`, `dependsOn`, `requires`, `required`, `taskClass`, `contextBudget`, `inputs`, `authorizedScope`, and `unresolvedAssumptions`. Unknown keys, missing dependencies, and cycles are refused before execution.
+
+## Commands
+
+```text
+/batch <spec-file>
+/batch run <spec-file>
+/batch validate <spec-file>
+/batch status [id]
+/batch list
+/batch pause [id]
+/batch resume [id]
+/batch cancel [id]
+/batch results [id]
+```
+
+Paths may be quoted or backslash-escaped and must resolve to a regular file inside the selected workspace. The file is limited to 256 KiB. `run` is sequential by default. To request parallel units, set `policy.maxConcurrentUnits` and `git.isolate: true`; the existing operation engine checks model/resource eligibility, dependencies, resource slot limits, and serialized verified integration. Without isolated worktrees, the existing spec validator refuses unsafe parallel limits.
+
+When an ID is omitted, a single active batch is selected. Multiple active batches require an explicit ID; if none is active, a sole batch is selected only when that is unambiguous. `/batch list` shows the available IDs. `status` shows progress; `results` shows each task's status, summary, and recorded verifier state. A blocked required task prevents `COMPLETE`; aggregate output reports `PARTIAL`, `BLOCKED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELLED` as derived from the durable operation record.
+
+The operation scheduler continues independent work while dependencies remain blocked. Retry, provider recovery, and restart use the existing operation decisions and state. Cancellation of an active `/batch run` uses the same signal as `/team`; a separate cancel request refuses an unsettled stored unit until recovery can classify it.
+
+## Current implementation boundary
+
+This is a staged v1.3.0 trail. `pause` is not implemented because the current durable operation schema has no distinct `PAUSED` state; the command returns an explicit unsupported-state response. A cancelled batch can be resumed from its durable record. `/loop`, `/goal`, independent acceptance review, and the requested minimal-provider end-to-end fixtures are not supplied by this batch slice.

+# PA-4 transient delegation authority milestone
+
+This milestone narrows the existing in-turn `spawn_subagent` path. It does not introduce another scheduler or durable store.
+
+## Contract
+
+- The compatible prompt-only call selects `semantic_explorer`, a predefined read-only profile.
+- Optional `profile` selects only an existing role; optional `inputs` accepts string values and conveys task data, never authority.
+- Unknown fields, unknown profiles, non-string inputs, and oversized requests are rejected before child construction.
+- Child tools are the intersection of the parent's currently offered tools, explicit matching parent grants (when configured), and the selected profile's allowlist. The dispatcher repeats this exact-name check before any tool effect.
+- A child has `fullAccess: false`; a writable profile requires an already established isolated worktree. Delegation depth is limited to one child level and each parent admits at most four child attempts.
+- Completion returns a validated structured receipt. An incomplete child with workspace mutations is `UNKNOWN_EFFECT`; a reported failure is not treated as completion.
+- The child uses its own conversation and returns only a bounded summary receipt to the parent. Parent cancellation continues to signal the child.
+
+These restrictions preserve prompt-only compatibility while intentionally refusing legacy prompt-only requests that relied on unrestricted writes. The current transient path has a per-parent child-attempt ceiling and depth bound; process-wide aggregate resource accounting and independent evidence review remain open PA-4 work.
+
+## Reference coding
+
+XERJ was consulted per `docs/XERJ_REFERENCE_CODING.md`. The useful reference was the peer pattern of host-owned predefined role profiles with allowlisted tools. No peer implementation was copied. XERJ field report was submitted after preview; GitHub PR creation was unavailable and the report endpoint accepted the fallback.

# PA-1 explicit execution resource admission

Status: implementation slice in progress; this document records the intended contract and evidence after the current code changes are verified.

## Contract

Durable operations may opt into parallel execution with `policy.maxConcurrentUnits > 1`. Every such operation must declare an operation-local `policy.executionBudget` and every work unit must declare `executionResources`:

```json
{
  "policy": {
    "maxConcurrentUnits": 3,
    "executionBudget": { "cpuMilli": 3000, "memoryBytes": 2147483648 }
  },
  "units": [
    { "id": "one", "prompt": "...", "executionResources": { "cpuMilli": 1000, "memoryBytes": 536870912 } }
  ]
}
```

`cpuMilli` is an operator-provided reservation in thousandths of a core. `memoryBytes` is an operator-provided reservation in bytes. These values are admission declarations, not provider telemetry, observed usage, or enforced operating-system quotas. A unit is admitted only when its declared CPU and memory fit alongside currently running declarations, the unit-count limit, provider concurrency slots, capability qualification, dependencies, and workspace isolation.

The operation count limit, provider request slots, and declared CPU/memory reservations are separate constraints. The scheduler does not infer CPU or memory limits from provider names, model identity, hardware count, or absent metadata. Serial execution remains available without resource declarations.

## Compatibility and failure behavior

Operation schema v4 records explicit resource reservations. Older operation records migrate additively; if they requested parallel execution without reservations, their effective concurrency is clamped to one with a warning. New parallel operation specifications missing a budget or any unit reservation are rejected before state creation. A request larger than the operation budget is also rejected. Single-unit operations do not need reservations.

These reservations cannot protect the host from a subprocess that exceeds its declared demand. Hard CPU or memory limits require a separately implemented execution boundary and are not claimed here.

# Nexus Code TUI audit — snapshot and diff views

Scope: `core/src/bin/nexus_tui.rs`, `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/diff_view.rs`, and the shared terminal color-depth adapter. This is a terminal-oriented adaptation of the Impeccable technical audit; the bundled browser detector and the iOS/Android audit do not apply to Ratatui.

| # | Dimension | Score | Key finding |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | Accessibility | 3/4 | Keyboard controls and non-color status labels/glyphs are present; ANSI 256-color text can become too faint on a light terminal background. Screen-reader and physical-terminal palettes were not measured. |
| 2 | Performance | 4/4 | Rendering has bounded layout and Unicode handling; the exact-head TUI test binary passes 394 tests. |
| 3 | Theming | 2/4 | Neutral 256-color diff text is hard-coded to pale indexed colors while its background follows the terminal. |
| 4 | Responsive design | 3/4 | Minimum dimensions and short-wide/wide-tall layouts are implemented and tested; one undersize message names the wrong dimension for short terminals. |
| 5 | Implementation integrity | 3/4 | Snapshot behavior has current source-fingerprint and PTY evidence; the latest diff-view palette change has no current PTY or screenshot capture. |
| **Total** | | **15/20** | **Good** |

## Implementation integrity verdict

**Pass with one important contrast defect and a current-render evidence gap.** The TUI uses terminal-default neutral surfaces, keyboard-first navigation, explicit diff markers, safe visible rendering of control and bidi characters, and a shared depth policy for snapshot rendering. The ANSI 256-color diff palette still assumes a dark background for neutral text.

## Executive summary

- Score: **15/20 (Good)**.
- Findings: **P0 0 / P1 1 / P2 0 / P3 2**.
- The previous snapshot-view audit is still current for `core/src/bin/nexus_tui.rs`: its SHA-256 remains `888b10968367e04977e33142cf28cb5340583dca03dd5490e28391432d13135f`, matching the 2026-11-20 report. That report recorded a 100×30 PTY check: `NO_COLOR=1 TERM=dumb` emitted no color SGR, and a color-capable PTY emitted color SGR.
- The diff palette changed later. Existing `docs/reviews/evidence/tui_diff` screenshots identify source head `88e070070e93d1dda5b5b842a4fb35da86be4b51`, so they do not qualify the current diff renderer at `073e6ea90b025acbd19f0c1b92ea1c9e93e6937e`.

## Findings

### P1 — ANSI 256-color diff text is too pale on light terminal backgrounds

- **Location:** `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/diff_view.rs:308-328`.
- **Category:** Accessibility / Theming.
- **Impact:** In 256-color mode, neutral diff text uses indexed color 254 (`#e4e4e4`) and metadata uses 247 (`#9e9e9e`) while context/code rows retain the terminal's default background. Against a common white terminal background, these are approximately 1.25:1 and 2.68:1 contrast respectively. Diff context and line numbers become difficult to read.
- **Recommendation:** Keep neutral text on `Color::Reset` and use indexed colors only where an explicit add/delete background provides a known pairing, or provide a tested light/dark palette choice. Retain `+`/`−` and line-number cues so color never carries the meaning alone.
- **Suggested command:** `$impeccable colorize`.

### P3 — Short-terminal recovery copy says “wider” when height is the constraint

- **Location:** `core/src/bin/nexus_tui.rs:272-275`.
- **Category:** Responsive design / UX copy.
- **Impact:** A wide terminal shorter than 14 rows receives “needs a wider terminal,” although the message's `58×14` minimum also hints at the real constraint.
- **Recommendation:** Use dimension-neutral wording such as “Nexus needs a terminal at least 58 columns × 14 rows.”
- **Suggested command:** `$impeccable adapt`.

### P3 — Current diff palette lacks rendered PTY evidence

- **Location:** `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/diff_view.rs:304-329`; stale screenshots are listed in `docs/reviews/evidence/tui_diff/tui_diff.manifest.json`.
- **Category:** Implementation integrity.
- **Impact:** Unit tests verify palette values and layout but do not show how the latest 256-color output reads on light and dark terminal backgrounds. The older screenshots predate the current palette commit.
- **Recommendation:** Capture the current diff view in a PTY at 256-color and truecolor depths, on both light and dark terminal palettes, and retain the output with the exact source head.
- **Suggested command:** `$impeccable audit`.

## Patterns and positive findings

- Neutral surfaces generally use terminal defaults, and diff meaning remains available through `+`/`−` markers and line numbers.
- Snapshot rendering shares `theme::Depth` handling, including monochrome behavior and ANSI 16-color SGR rewriting.
- Snapshot layout adapts between stacked and side-by-side modes based on both width and height.
- The current TUI test suite covers narrow layouts, Unicode cell widths, control/bidi text safety, color depth, and monochrome selection behavior.

## Recommended actions

1. **[P1] `$impeccable colorize`**: Fix ANSI 256-color neutral text contrast on light terminal backgrounds.
2. **[P3] `$impeccable adapt`**: Correct the minimum-size recovery message for height-constrained terminals.
3. **[P3] `$impeccable audit`**: Capture current diff-view PTY output for 256-color and truecolor on light and dark palettes.
4. **`$impeccable polish`**: Recheck the full TUI path after fixes and captures.

## Remaining limitations

- No physical terminal or screen-reader test was run in this pass.
- ANSI 16-color output follows the operator's configured palette, so contrast can vary by terminal configuration.
- The browser detector cannot inspect Ratatui terminal applications.

content.text: The merged `/batch` lifecycle is already wired to durable operations. Legacy objectives will carry an explicit “earlier count unknown” marker.

+# PA-3 durable goal lifecycle
+
+This slice adds `/goal` as a durable objective lifecycle over `TeamOrchestrator`, `OperationStore`, and the existing
+`ObjectiveLedger`. It does not add another scheduler or workflow store. The original objective and its requirement
+ledger live in the operation's existing durable task record; operation transitions preserve that ledger. Work-unit
+ledgers remain attached to their own durable tasks and contribute only requirement evidence for the same immutable
+objective.
+
+## Commands
+
+```text
+/goal <objective>
+/goal status [id]
+/goal list
+/goal show <id>
+/goal pause [id]
+/goal resume [id]
+/goal cancel [id]
+/goal requirements [id]
+/goal requirements descope <goal-id> <requirement-id> <reason>
+/goal requirements accept <goal-id> <requirement-id>
+/goal evidence [id]
+```
+
+Omitting an id selects the only active goal, or the only goal in the workspace. Multiple eligible goals require an
+explicit id. Scope reduction records a reason first and requires a separate operator acceptance command, using the
+existing objective-ledger `applyRequirementUpdates` and `acceptDescoping` rules.
+
+## Acceptance and recovery
+
+A goal is `COMPLETE` only when its durable operation completed, the independent reviewer produced an accepted verdict
+on a model distinct from the implementer, deterministic verification passed with executed tests, and the parent
+objective ledger has no open or unaccepted requirements. Review depends on the tester unit so it sees the candidate
+after verification. Missing evidence, a failed review, or an unresolved hard requirement remains `BLOCKED`.
+
+Pause and cancellation refuse to overwrite a running unit. The operator resumes first so the operation runner can
+reconcile any unknown effect. A cancelled goal is terminal. A process restart retains the operation graph, work-unit
+task ids, objective ledger and receipts through the existing operation/task store.
+
+The command handler is shared by the REPL and sidecar router; the TUI receives it from the sidecar catalogue. The REPL
+marks status/list/show/requirements/evidence as read-only inspection and keeps execution, pause, resume, cancel and
+scope changes unavailable in read-only mode.
+
+## Current limits
+
+- Goal decomposition currently reuses the existing full team graph; arbitrary requirement-to-work-unit mapping is not
+  exposed by `/goal`. Use `/batch` when an operator needs an authored work-unit DAG.
+- This is a PA-3/PA-4 implementation slice. `/loop`, expanded goal decomposition, restart-specific paused boot
+  identity, lifecycle interface tests, and the complete PA-4 qualification matrix remain open.
+- No inference-provider or homelab-ai changes are required. Provider-neutral end-to-end qualification remains separate.
+
+## Reference coding
+
+XERJ returned the opencode goal-state pattern of bounded rounds and a server boot identity at
+`packages/schema/src/goal.ts:11`, plus restart-pausing behavior in `packages/core/src/plugin/goal.ts:339`. These informed
+the recovery questions only; no peer code was copied. XERJ marked the corpus as incompletely indexed, so absence of a
+result is not evidence that no other pattern exists.
*** End Patch";

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > docs/v1.3.0/PA4_LOOP_LIFECYCLE.md <<'EOF'
# PA-4: bounded `/loop` lifecycle

## Architecture

`/loop` stores its controller receipt in the existing durable task state (`DurableTaskState.loop`) and stores each attempt as a child operation in the existing `OperationStore`. Work is scheduled by `driveOperation` and the existing convergence scheduler. The loop does not create a second task graph or provider client. Loop state has its own schema version so existing task schema version 2 records remain readable without migration.

A child attempt is a `/team full` operation with a deterministic tester and the existing independent reviewer. The reviewer depends on the verifier. Completion requires the operation to finish, the verifier receipt to report executed tests and `PASSED`, and the independent reviewer receipt to say `ACCEPT`; artifact conditions additionally require a regular file whose real path remains inside the workspace. Agent statements cannot satisfy a deterministic verifier condition.

Only provider-reported token totals are placed in `reportedTokens`. Mixed or estimated request totals go in `estimatedTokens`; inference request counts are recorded only when available from the durable child task. Missing child accounting remains zero and is not presented as a measurement.

## Command grammar

Options must precede the objective. Arguments use the shared shell-like word parser: single or double quotes group whitespace, backslash escapes the next character, and unmatched quotes or a trailing escape are rejected. Unicode text is preserved. The first word is reserved for lifecycle actions (`status`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `stop`), so an objective beginning with one of those words must be quoted as a single objective argument after a harmless prefix, for example `/loop "status the new behavior"` is still treated as the status action; use `/loop objective: status the new behavior`.

```text
/loop [--until <condition>] [--max-iterations <n>] [--max-duration <duration>] <objective>
/loop status [id]
/loop list
/loop pause [id]
/loop resume [id]
/loop stop [id]
```

Conditions are one quoted token:

- `test=<command>` requires the verifier receipt to match that exact command.
- `artifact=<relative-path>::<command>` requires the matching verifier and a regular artifact under the workspace (symlink escapes are refused).
- `criteria=<text>` gives criteria to the independent reviewer; it still requires a passing deterministic test receipt.

Duration values are positive integers followed by `ms`, `s`, `m`, or `h`. The minimum is one second and the maximum is 24 hours. The default is three iterations and one hour. Iterations are bounded to 1..100. Repeating an option uses its last value. Unknown options, malformed numbers, unknown conditions, and missing values are errors. Maximum iterations and duration produce `EXHAUSTED`, never `COMPLETE`.

When an ID is omitted, exactly one active loop is selected; otherwise an error asks for the ID. If no loop is active, a sole historical loop can be inspected. Multiple historical loops require an explicit ID. `pause` takes effect at a durable child-operation boundary. Ctrl-C requests the same safe-boundary pause. `stop` requests cancellation and is acknowledged after the current operation settles; it does not assert that a running external effect was undone.

A child operation found with a stale `RUNNING` unit is marked `UNKNOWN_EFFECT` and is not replayed. A child cancellation is converted to a durable unknown-effect block because the current shared scheduler maps cancelled units back to runnable; this prevents `/loop` from repeatedly invoking an uncertain effect. Resume refuses unknown-effect loops. The underlying scheduler cancellation behavior is recorded as a boundary request for the PA-1 owner.

## Integration and evidence

The shared slash catalogue feeds command completion in terminal interfaces. The REPL and sidecar call the same `executeLoopCommand`; read-only mode permits only `status` and `list`. State records retain bounded summaries, verifier/reviewer receipts, operation references, fingerprints, and usage labels, not the child transcript. Detailed child evidence remains in the existing durable operation records.

Focused lifecycle coverage is in `cli/test/loop_lifecycle.test.ts`; task schema and migration coverage remains in `cli/test/state_migration.test.ts`. Local run evidence is recorded in the implementation PR and may be updated after the release branch is rebased.

const body = `## Problem
The default Bubblewrap verifier still returned \`VERIFIED\` when candidate product code read an unchanged baseline test file to obtain its expected result. I reproduced this with the hostile fixture: the tests failed on the base, passed on the candidate, and the receipt claimed independent verification.

## Fix
- Trace verifier file opens outside the Bubblewrap namespace using the system \`strace\` binary; never resolve the tracer from workspace-controlled PATH.
- Compare candidate reads of baseline test files with the base-run counts. An additional read marks independence false, records the path in \`runs[].testFixtureReads\`, and caps the verdict at \`REGRESSION_FREE\`.
- If the trace cannot be collected (Docker-only hosts, missing tracer, or unreadable trace), fail closed to \`REGRESSION_FREE\`.
- Keep the explicit \`--sandbox none\` trusted-input opt-out behavior.
- Update the v2 receipt schema and docs.

## Validation
- Reproduced the original false \`VERIFIED\` on the default Bubblewrap path before the fix.
- Hostile verifier suite: 30/30.
- Focused default attack and ordinary-fix checks: 2/2; the malicious candidate is \`REGRESSION_FREE\` and an ordinary fix remains \`VERIFIED\`.
- Sandbox: 9/9; command: 18/18; type-check/guard: 13/13; action: 9/9; schema: 4/4.
- \`npm --prefix cli run build\`: passed.
- \`node cli/scripts/gen_verify_result_schema.mjs --check\`: passed.
- All TypeScript test invocations used throwaway HOME directories.

## Reference coding
Queried the local OpenCode corpus for independent test-oracle isolation and runtime file tracing. It returned no directly applicable implementation; no code was copied or borrowed. The design is based on the reproduced Nexus behavior and fails closed when OS tracing is unavailable. The required XERJ field report was submitted.

## Limits
Runtime oracle-access tracing is available for Bubblewrap on Linux with system \`strace\`. Docker-only and other hosts cannot claim independent verification through this path and return at most \`REGRESSION_FREE\`. This does not prove that finite tests cover the full specification.`;

+# PA-4 comparative workflow evaluation
+
+Status: protocol implemented; development-harness tests pass; comparative inference results and held-out qualification are pending.
+
+## Scope and arms
+
+The harness compares identical versioned tasks through five bounded Nexus execution paths:
+
+1. **Serial:** the existing single-agent `nexus run` adapter.
+2. **Independent agents:** one parent turn requests three separate read-only subagent analyses before doing the unchanged objective.
+3. **Specialist-assisted:** `/team full --independent-review <objective>`.
+4. **Durable goal:** `/goal <objective>`.
+5. **Bounded batch:** `/batch <generated-spec>` with a sequential research, design, implementation, verification, and review graph.
+
+Each arm reuses `eval/run.mjs`, its isolated model proxy, workspace and HOME creation, task snapshots, hidden evaluators, and result receipts. Workflow commands run through the same sidecar protocol used by terminal clients. The generated batch specification is removed after execution; the durable operation state and individual unit receipts remain in the run HOME. The ordinary serial arm stays on the standard one-shot CLI adapter.
+
+## Controls and scoring
+
+The input provider config, dataset digest, task objective, budgets, model, context/output limits, and sampling are common to all arms. Each run receives a fresh isolated workspace and HOME. Arm order rotates by task and replicate. Failed and interrupted runs retain their logs and are included in the denominator. The evaluator verifies the same deterministic artifact and regression criteria after each arm.
+
+The score reports acceptance first, then wall time and inference request counts. An arm with lower observed acceptance than serial is not eligible for efficiency promotion. Token fields retain runner provenance; estimates remain estimates, and absent telemetry remains unavailable. A comparison does not establish improvement from latency or throughput alone.
+
+## Evidence and limits
+
+Local deterministic tests cover arm mapping, operation-spec graph construction, Unicode/objective retention, and sidecar terminal-receipt handling. No inference comparison was run while the repository's GATEWAY claim was held by another workstream. The harness refuses `qualification: true`: this implementation is a repeatable development protocol, not held-out evidence. It does not claim measured comparative outcomes, security qualification, or acceptance superiority. A separately authorized held-out run and independent review remain required.
+
+## Reproduction
+
+See `eval/README.md`, section “PA-4 orchestration comparison (development protocol),” for commands and required inputs. Each output directory has a pinned dataset/config manifest, per-arm runner manifests and raw logs, `runs.jsonl`, and an aggregate score generated with `eval/score_workflows.mjs`.

+3. **Specialist-assisted:** `/team full --independent-review <objective>`.

content.text:
Implement a production-grade context maturity system in Nexus Code, grounded in the Redis “Context Engineering Maturity Model” (/home/mike/Redis_ePub_Ebook_ContextMaturityModel_260522.pdf) but adapted to Nexus’s actual architecture. Treat that document as a diagnostic framework, not a vendor blueprint. Do not assume Nexus should use Redis, MCP, a vector database, or any other specific product unless the existing code and measured requirements justify it.

## Objective

Make Nexus’s context capabilities explicit, inspectable, and incrementally improvable across four dimensions:

1. Navigability: agents can find and relate relevant repository, task, session, and memory context.
2. Retrieval speed: context assembly has measurable latency, budgets, and failure behavior.
3. Freshness: the system can determine whether context reflects current repository and session state.
4. Compounding value: useful knowledge can persist across turns and sessions under controlled scope, provenance, and retention rules.

Use the model’s five maturity stages as descriptive assessment levels:

1. Ad hoc
2. Exploratory
3. Standardizing
4. Managed
5. Competitive asset

Do not collapse the four dimensions into a single maturity score. Assess each dimension separately, report the evidence and gaps behind each rating, and identify the next implementable improvement. Do not claim a stage based only on feature presence.

## Operating constraints

- First confirm that the active repository is Nexus Code. If it is not, stop without modifying files and report the repository identity.
- Inspect the current implementation, docs, roadmap, session export format, memory/context mechanisms, agent profiles, command system, and test conventions before designing changes.
- Preserve Nexus’s provider independence. The context system must work through existing provider interfaces and must not require provider-specific customization.
- Preserve local inference as the preferred default and cloud fallback only when required by existing policy.
- Keep context assembly in Nexus’s client/control plane. Do not make inference providers responsible for Nexus memory, state, or context policy.
- Maintain Nexus’s priority order: accurate task completion first, useful evidence and observability second, presentation and UX third.
- Treat repository files, prompts, model output, tool output, and stored memory as untrusted input unless validated.
- “Memory is not evidence.” A model-generated summary or remembered claim must not become verified fact without source evidence.
- Do not add Redis or another service dependency by default. Prefer the smallest architecture that meets demonstrated requirements.
- Avoid broad rewrites. Preserve existing user data, session records, and backward compatibility where practical.
- Do not overwrite unrelated working tree changes. Record the initial branch, commit, and worktree status; keep changes scoped to this task.
- Make routine implementation decisions independently. Do not stop for approval unless blocked by a destructive or externally consequential operation.

## Phase 1: Baseline and design

1. Map the current context lifecycle:
   - sources and source adapters
   - context selection and assembly
   - token budgeting and truncation
   - session and cross-session persistence
   - task/profile/path-scoped context
   - retrieval and ranking
   - provider request construction
   - exported session evidence
2. Identify existing guarantees and gaps against all four dimensions and five stages.
3. Build a Nexus-specific capability matrix. Each rating must cite implementation evidence or explicitly say “not measured” / “not implemented.” Separate current behavior from planned behavior.
4. Write a short design decision record before implementation, including:
   - proposed data model and interfaces
   - compatibility and migration approach
   - security, privacy, retention, and failure considerations
   - measurable acceptance criteria
   - what is intentionally deferred and why

Do not pause after producing the assessment. Continue into implementation unless the repository is not Nexus Code or a concrete blocker makes safe implementation impossible.

## Phase 2: Implement the minimum coherent system

Adapt the following capabilities to Nexus’s existing abstractions. Do not duplicate functionality that already exists; extend or connect existing components where possible.

### A. Context inventory and provenance

Represent assembled context as inspectable items with, as applicable:

- stable item identifier
- source type and source location
- scope: turn, session, task, repository/worktree, profile, or user
- content or content reference
- created/observed/validated timestamps
- freshness or invalidation rule
- trust/verification state
- retention or expiry rule
- reason for inclusion and retrieval method

Preserve source references in session records and exports. Avoid logging secrets or copying sensitive content into diagnostics.

### B. Navigability

Create or extend a common context retrieval interface that can combine relevant existing sources, such as:

- current task and acceptance criteria
- active session state and prior steps
- repository status, changed files, and relevant code/docs
- path-scoped rules and agent profile instructions
- explicitly approved durable memories
- prior evidence or decisions when relevant

Use structured relationships and metadata where Nexus already has them. Do not expose raw database or filesystem access to a model when an existing controlled interface can answer the request. Make retrieval reasons inspectable.

### C. Freshness and invalidation

Define freshness separately for each context source. At minimum, handle:

- changed repository/worktree state
- changed files or rules
- session transitions, resume, and compaction
- stale cached retrieval results
- memories whose source or validation status has changed

Do not imply that a context item is current when Nexus cannot establish that. Surface unknown freshness as unknown. Ensure resume and compaction preserve source links and do not silently convert summaries into authoritative state.

### D. Retrieval performance and budgets

Add instrumentation for context assembly and retrieval, using existing telemetry conventions:

- duration by source and overall
- result count and omission count
- token or size estimates where available
- cache hit/miss and invalidation reason where applicable
- timeout, partial-result, and error outcomes

Define configurable budgets and deterministic behavior when budgets are exceeded. A timeout or failed source must be represented explicitly; do not silently treat incomplete context as complete. Avoid caching sensitive context across scopes or users.

### E. Controlled durable memory

Implement or extend memory only where the current architecture supports it safely. Distinguish:

- ephemeral working context
- session history and summaries
- durable project/repository knowledge
- user/profile preferences, if already supported

For every durable memory item, retain provenance, scope, validation status, timestamp, and retention/expiry metadata. Provide a controlled promotion path from interaction to durable memory. Do not automatically promote model assertions, unverified tool output, credentials, secrets, or transient task details. Ensure retrieval respects scope and deletion/expiry rules.

### F. Maturity assessment

Provide a machine-readable and human-readable assessment of the four dimensions. Each assessment must include:

- current level, or “insufficient evidence”
- evidence references
- unmet criteria
- known limitations
- next actionable improvement

The assessment must be reproducible from system state and recorded evidence, not generated as an unsupported model opinion. If a CLI command, report, or UI view already exists for diagnostics, integrate there. Otherwise choose the smallest consistent interface and document it.

## Phase 3: Validation and delivery

Add focused tests for the new behavior and failure cases, following existing test patterns. Cover at least:

- source provenance surviving context assembly, compaction, resume, and export
- stale or invalidated context being detected or explicitly marked unknown
- source timeout/failure producing an incomplete-context signal
- scope isolation for memory and context
- rejection or quarantine of unverified durable-memory promotion
- deterministic token/size budget behavior
- assessment output backed by evidence, including “insufficient evidence”
- compatibility with more than one provider adapter, if the repository has multiple adapters

Run the relevant targeted tests and required repository checks. Do not claim broader validation than was actually run. Do not change tests to hide regressions.

At completion, report:

1. initial and final branch/commit/worktree status
2. implemented behavior and key files changed
3. maturity assessment before and after, with evidence
4. tests/checks run and exact results
5. limitations, deferred work, migration concerns, and operational risks
6. any remaining acceptance gaps

Do not claim Nexus reached a maturity stage unless the evidence meets that stage’s criteria. The goal is a working, auditable context system with a defensible baseline and clear next steps, not a maturity label.

I’m switching to the context-system task and will preserve the verification PR work as-is. I’ll first confirm the repository and working-tree state, then inspect the existing context/session/memory paths and the maturity-model document before choosing a bounded implementation slice.

content.text: The checkout is Nexus Code at clean `main` commit `9156571f`; I’ve created an isolated worktree for this task. The baseline already has substantial context machinery—token admission, compaction/archive recovery, skills, search, and persistent project knowledge—but those pieces do not yet share a complete per-item provenance and freshness view. A hot file needed for automatic per-inference capture is actively claimed by another workstream, so I’m building the independent inventory, maturity report, session/export persistence, and shared slash-command surface first, without crossing that file boundary.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-system/docs/research/context-engineering/CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md
+# Nexus context maturity and inventory
+
+Status: implementation record for the context maturity system. This is a diagnostic and observability layer over existing Nexus context behavior; it does not replace the agent's request construction or token-admission policy.
+
+## Baseline
+
+Repository: Nexus Code, `main` at `9156571f7d5fd8f8436c3105f0237628ab35e857`, clean at inspection on 2026-11-22. Implementation is isolated in `codex/context-maturity-system`.
+
+The reference is *The Context Engineering Maturity Model: A Framework for Building Production-Ready Agentic Systems* (Redis, 2025/2026 ebook), especially its four pillars and five descriptive stages (pp. 7–16). Nexus uses four dimensions requested for this assessment and adapts the stage language to a local coding client. Vendor architecture recommendations are not treated as implementation requirements.
+
+| Dimension | Baseline level | Evidence and observed behavior | Gaps and limitations | Next improvement |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Navigability | 2 — Exploratory | `AutonomousAgent.requestMessages` carries conversation and pins the durable objective (`cli/src/agent.ts:2283-2303`); `getContextBudget` accounts for messages and tool schemas (`agent.ts:2440-2443`); repository search, skills, and `KnowledgeGraph` exist (`cli/src/knowledge.ts:37-45`, `cli/src/skills.ts:498-518`). | These sources do not have a shared inspectable inventory; the prompt combines several sources and history is replayed as messages. Retrieval reasons and cross-source relationships are not reported together. | Add a common inventory format and a read-only inspection command, while explicitly listing uncovered sources. |
+| Retrieval speed | 2 — Exploratory | Deterministic client token estimates, provider-advertised counts where available, admission and bounded compaction exist (`cli/src/tokens.ts:97-158`, `cli/src/agent.ts:3375-3472`). | No source-level retrieval latency budget or SLO is recorded. Admission logs do not measure time spent assembling each source; estimates are not provider measurements. | Record per-source and total inventory-assembly duration; keep it distinct from inference latency and token estimates. |
+| Freshness | 1 — Ad hoc | Context is gathered from the live session; candidate/verification evidence has identity-based invalidation elsewhere in the execution model. | Ordinary transcript/tool observations do not consistently carry a repository fingerprint or invalidation rule. Persisted knowledge has timestamps but no enforced applicability fingerprint. Unknown freshness can look current if rendered as prose. | Attach explicit freshness state and source references; report `unknown` where no applicable fingerprint exists. |
+| Compounding value | 2 — Exploratory | Sessions, compaction archives and durable task state persist across process restarts (`cli/src/session.ts:102-184`); project knowledge persists in `.nexus/knowledge.json` (`cli/src/knowledge.ts:37-45`). | Session history, task summaries, and repository knowledge have different scopes but no unified provenance/retention view. Knowledge auto-extraction is opt-in and trust-gated, but a stored entry is not evidence of correctness. | Preserve source-only inventory metadata in session records and exports; do not elevate model or tool claims to verified facts. |
+
+Ratings are per dimension. There is no aggregate maturity grade. A feature's presence alone does not satisfy a stage: the report requires evidence for shared behavior, freshness, and measured service levels.
+
+## Design decision record
+
+### Decision
+
+Add a small, local context inventory and deterministic maturity assessment that reuse `AutonomousAgent` getters, `DurableTaskState`/`SessionManager`, existing token estimates, `KnowledgeGraph`, and the common slash router. The inventory stores metadata and hashes, not prompt plaintext. Existing provider adapters remain the only inference transport boundary; this feature does not call providers.
+
+### Data model and interfaces
+
+- `ContextInventoryItem`: stable content-derived id, source kind/location, scope, hash, estimated size/tokens, observed time, freshness (`current`, `stale`, `unknown`), trust state, retention, inclusion reason, retrieval method, and optional source references.
+- `ContextInventorySnapshot`: schema version, capture time, session/task/workspace identity, item list, per-source timing/status/counts, estimate provenance, omissions, completeness, and reason for incomplete or unknown coverage.
+- The persisted snapshot is optional. Older session records remain valid and are reconstructed as `unknown`/partial on read; they are never reinterpreted as fresh.
+- `context inspect [--json]` displays the current inspectable inventory; `context maturity [--json]` emits a reproducible four-dimension assessment with evidence, gaps, limitations, and next improvements.
+
+### Compatibility, security, privacy, and retention
+
+- Existing message and session schemas remain readable. New metadata is additive and source-only; full message and tool content remains in the existing session/archive path.
+- Hashes and locators are diagnostic provenance, not proof that a tool observation is true. Model output is labeled model-generated; tool output is labeled unverified unless an existing verifier receipt binds it.
+- No secret-bearing source text is copied into the inventory or maturity report. Paths are workspace-relative where possible. Inventory snapshots follow the containing session's existing retention/deletion behavior; no cross-user cache is introduced.
+- Workspace changes do not silently make an old observation current. If Nexus has no compatible source fingerprint, freshness remains `unknown`.
+- Inventory collection is local and read-only. Failed or unsupported sources are reported with explicit partial status.
+
+### Acceptance criteria
+
+1. The same session state yields the same item identities, estimates, assessment levels, and evidence ordering (capture timestamps and duration metrics are the only variable fields).
+2. Inventory content contains no source plaintext and distinguishes operator, model, tool, and persisted-knowledge trust states.
+3. Compaction and resume retain source references or mark reconstructed provenance and freshness as unknown; exports carry the inventory and archive references.
+4. Source errors and item/token caps are visible as incomplete with counts; no partial inventory is called complete.
+5. Context inspection and maturity assessment are available through the shared REPL/TUI slash router and JSON output is parseable.
+6. A schema-less/legacy session remains loadable and receives conservative reconstructed inventory metadata.
+7. No provider changes, provider-specific headers, or new service dependencies are added.
+
+### Deferred work
+
+- Per-inference inventory capture at request construction and admission, plus context-manifest persistence, requires the currently claimed `cli/src/agent.ts` slice. No edits are made to that file while its owner is active. The diagnostic reports this capture gap explicitly; a follow-up integration must claim the file and preserve this record format.
+- Automatic durable-memory promotion, retrieval ranking changes, and context eviction remain deferred. Existing validation research (`CONTEXT-ENGINEERING-VALIDATION-PLAN.md`) says to validate bounded ingestion and evidence reuse before adopting more complex retrieval policies.
+- No Redis, MCP server, vector database, new provider extension, or autonomous memory learner is justified by measured requirements.
+
+## Reference coding
+
+XERJ retrieval on `nexus-cli` located the existing context admission/token-accounting path in `cli/src/agent.ts` (`requestMessages`, `admitContext`) and the durable note provenance logic in the same file, plus the project knowledge graph in `cli/src/knowledge.ts`. The implementation reuses those boundaries and adds a local diagnostic; it rejects adding a second planner, a provider-specific context protocol, or an external retrieval service. XERJ's index reflects committed `origin/main`, so current worktree details were checked directly in source. No reference-project code was copied.
*** End Patch";

## Status: `PARTIAL_BLOCKED`

The context inventory and maturity diagnostic are implemented on a local worktree based on `release/v1.3.0`. I’m not calling the system complete: the exact inference-request manifest and a safe durable-memory promotion gate both need changes in files held by an active GV-1 owner.

### Implementation and assessment

Added `/context inspect [--json] [--record]` and `/context maturity [--json]` to the shared slash-command catalogue and REPL dispatch. The inventory records source references, scope, trust, freshness, retrieval reason, client-estimated tokens, timings, and omissions without storing source text. Optional metadata survives session save/resume and appears in session exports with archive references. Read-only inspection is allowed; recording remains disallowed in read-only mode.

| Dimension | Baseline | Observed command fixture | Evidence and remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Navigability | Stage 2 — Exploratory | Stage 2 — Exploratory | Inventory and source references are inspectable; exact per-inference context and relationships among prompt components are missing. |
| Retrieval speed | Stage 2 — Exploratory | Stage 2 — Exploratory | Local source timings are recorded. There is no source deadline, per-inference latency distribution, or retrieval SLO. |
| Freshness | Stage 1 — Ad hoc | Stage 1 — Ad hoc | Historical context is marked unknown; repository fingerprinting and systematic invalidation are missing. |
| Compounding value | Stage 2 — Exploratory | Stage 1 — Ad hoc | The fixture contained no durable memory. The assessment rises to Stage 2 only when durable knowledge, notes, or compaction links are observed; promotion controls, expiry enforcement, and quality evidence remain absent. |

There is no combined maturity score. The baseline, design decisions, evidence, and limitations are documented in [CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/research/context-engineering/CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md).

### Files changed

The main additions are [context_inventory.ts](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/cli/src/core/context_inventory.ts) and [context_inventory.test.ts](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/cli/test/context_inventory.test.ts). I also updated session state and export handling, the slash catalogue and workspace handler, REPL help/dispatch, and the sidecar’s read-only command policy.

### Verification

- `npm --prefix cli run build` — passed.
- `context_inventory.test.ts` — 7 passed.
- `session_durable_fields.test.ts` — 4 passed.
- `session_export_escaping.test.ts` — 5 passed.
- `provider_wire_matrix.test.ts` — 90 passed across mock OpenAI Chat/Responses, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock-compatible, and operator-defined fixtures.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- The full repository suite and independent review were not run. Tests used Node 24.11.1 with isolated `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. The provider tests were mocks; no live inference occurred.

No provider was modified, no new service dependency was added, and local inference defaults were left unchanged.

### Remaining blockers

The active GV-1 slice owns `agent.ts`, `spine_handlers.ts`, and `index.ts`. I recorded two bounded handoff requests in the shared claims log:

1. Capture the exact context manifest during inference request assembly.
2. Prevent model-originated `manage_knowledge` writes and prompt-derived auto-extraction from promoting unverified content without operator confirmation.

Agent Mail could not deliver the request because the active owner has no registered identity there. No changes were made to those claimed files. These gaps, along with the lack of source timeout guarantees and memory expiry enforcement, prevent qualification as a production-complete system.

content.text:
Implemented the context-maturity system on **`release/v1.3.0`**. The original checkout was clean at `main` (`9156571f`); work stayed in the isolated `codex/context-maturity-v130` worktree.

The branch is clean at **`87f8b6f3`**, based on `origin/release/v1.3.0` (`ab7af749`), and is two commits ahead. The work is committed locally; it has not been pushed or opened as a PR.

**What changed:** Nexus now has `/context inspect` and `/context maturity`, content-free records of the exact message and tool-schema arrays handed to inference adapters, and bounded session persistence and export for those records. A request is recorded before dispatch; a configured persistence failure prevents dispatch. Failed or interrupted requests are marked `unknown_effect` on recovery. Durable memory uses explicit operator promotion, provenance and expiry controls. The new **CE-1 Context Engineering Maturity** trail is in the v1.3.0 plan.

**Maturity before and after:** The levels remain the same because the new evidence does not establish higher-stage criteria:

- **Navigability:** 2 — Exploratory. Request positions and tool schemas are now inspectable; semantic links back to all originating sources remain incomplete.
- **Retrieval speed:** 2 — Exploratory. Source and inventory timings are recorded; no retrieval SLO or latency distribution is established.
- **Freshness:** 1 — Ad hoc. Persisted observations become unknown until revalidated; systematic repository fingerprints are still missing.
- **Compounding value:** 1 — Ad hoc without carried memory, or 2 — Exploratory when durable notes or compaction links are observed. Held-out evidence of memory improving task outcomes is not available.

**Validation:** `npm run build` passed. Focused tests passed: context inventory 11/11, knowledge memory 3/3, persistence protection 27/27, slash router 39/39, durable session fields 4/4, export escaping 5/5, agent harness 90/90, and provider wire matrix 90/90. `git diff --check` passed. Tests ran one file at a time with isolated homes; the full repository suite was not run.

No inference-provider code was changed and no live provider was contacted. Existing local fixtures cover OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible and other adapter shapes. This confirms fixture compatibility, not provider receipt or internal provider-side processing of a request.

Independent review and full-suite qualification remain pending. Other open work includes source-to-request semantic links, systematic repository freshness invalidation, retrieval latency targets, and held-out memory-quality evaluation.

content.text:
## Delivery status: IMPLEMENTED_QUALIFICATION_PENDING

Implemented the context inventory, request manifests, repository freshness comparison, guarded memory promotion, `/context inspect`, and `/context maturity`. The implementation is local to `codex/context-maturity-v130`, rebased onto `release/v1.3.0` at `a57c6c24`. Final HEAD is `03b62aaf73bee1b7abe2787bad471564e1dfd38d`; the worktree is clean and six commits ahead of the release branch. Nothing was pushed or published.

## Assessment

The baseline and current four-dimension assessments, evidence, gaps, and next improvements are recorded in the [context maturity decision record](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/research/context-engineering/CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md). Current ratings remain:

- Navigability: **2 — Exploratory**
- Retrieval speed: **2 — Exploratory**
- Freshness: **1 — Ad hoc**
- Compounding value: **1 or 2 — Ad hoc / Exploratory**, depending on available durable context

No dimension was promoted based only on feature presence. The [v1.3.0 plan](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md) records the remaining qualification work.

## Implementation and provider compatibility

The implementation reuses Nexus’s agent request path, sessions and archives, `KnowledgeGraph`, token admission, and common slash routing. Manifests retain metadata and source references, not prompt text. Memory promotion is operator-controlled, provenance-bearing, and rejects model-originated promotion. Workspace freshness is compared using a bounded candidate fingerprint; missing or failed comparisons remain unknown.

No inference provider was modified or contacted for this feature. The existing mock adapter wire matrix passed across OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, and other adapter fixtures. This verifies adapter compatibility coverage, not end-to-end production inference.

## Verification

On the current source at `b588d970`, before the documentation-only final commit:

- `npm run build` — passed.
- `node --import tsx --test test/context_inventory.test.ts` — **14 passed**.
- `node --import tsx --test test/knowledge_memory_controls.test.ts` — **3 passed**.
- `node --import tsx --test test/provider_wire_matrix.test.ts` — **90 passed**.

A full `make test` attempt on snapshot `48bb93f2` failed: Rust core **53 passed**, TUI **406 passed**, CLI **1,796 completed with 117 failures and 2 timeouts**; scope fixtures and security gates passed. The run reported missing `harness-core` and `cli/dist` build outputs and core RPC handshake failures. After building and placing runtime outputs at the paths expected by the test harness, the full `turn_semantics` file passed **37/37**, and the focused long-step test passed **1/1**. The full suite was not rerun on the current rebased HEAD, and the 117 failures were not all individually attributed.

## Remaining gaps

Source-specific freshness beyond repository state, retrieval deadlines and latency distributions, held-out evidence of memory quality, an independent review, and a successful aggregate suite run remain outstanding. The changes and qualification evidence are in six local commits; review and release qualification are still pending.

content.text:
## Status: `IMPLEMENTED_QUALIFICATION_PENDING`

Implemented the context maturity system on `codex/context-maturity-v130`, based on `release/v1.3.0`. The worktree is clean at `06a578c86fea1e16475ad17069788537ced4e1bc`, eight commits ahead of `origin/release/v1.3.0`. No push or PR was created.

The implementation adds a content-free context inventory and inspection command, request manifests at adapter dispatch, bounded workspace freshness checks, provenance in session and export records, and controlled durable-memory promotion. Model-invoked knowledge writes are denied. The roadmap and design record are updated in [CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/research/context-engineering/CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md) and [PLAN.md](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md).

The evidence-backed ratings remain modest: **navigability 2 — Exploratory; retrieval speed 2 — Exploratory; freshness 1 — Ad hoc; compounding value 1 — Ad hoc in the no-memory fixture, or 2 — Exploratory when durable notes or compaction links are present.** No combined maturity score is claimed.

### Verification

On the rebased tree, `npm run build` passed. Focused tests passed: context inventory **14/14**, memory controls **3/3**, provider wire matrix **90/90**, and turn-verdict evidence **26/26**. The provider tests use local fixtures; no inference provider was changed.

The full `make test` run **failed overall**. Rust core passed **53/53**, and scope fixtures and security gates passed, but the sharded runner did not provide a reliable aggregate test count. Two evaluation cases failed closed because compiler-exposure inventory was unavailable. A version-probe retry using the designated runtime and private tmpfs then failed because bubblewrap could not access the workspace through the host’s `/tmp` parent path. These failures and the unavailable independent review are recorded in the design document.

Known gaps include unmeasured retrieval latency objectives, incomplete freshness coverage for non-repository sources and memory provenance, and no held-out evaluation of memory’s effect on task quality. The aggregate suite still needs qualification on a host where the evaluation fixtures work.

## Status: IMPLEMENTED_QUALIFICATION_PENDING

The context inventory and maturity assessment are implemented on `codex/context-maturity-v130`, targeting `release/v1.3.0`. The branch is clean at `1dad3fdf`, based on release head `cd755b3e`. It has not been pushed or opened as a PR; it is ready for Claude’s review.

The implementation adds `/context inspect` and `/context maturity`, content-free provenance for inference requests, bounded context collection with explicit timeout and omission reporting, freshness invalidation, and operator-only durable-memory promotion. Provider adapters and inference providers were not modified.

The design record and qualification evidence are in [CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/research/context-engineering/CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md). The four dimensions remain independently rated; the system does not claim an overall maturity score.

### Verification

On the rebased branch, `npm run build` passed and `test/context_inventory.test.ts` passed **16/16**. Before the release rebase, focused checks also passed for provider wire fixtures (**90/90**), slash routing (**39/39**), memory controls (**3/3**), persistence protection (**27/27**), and skill injection (**15/15**).

The corrected full `make test` run used snapshot `2502ae1b` based on `a5faa878`. Core tests (**53/53**), TUI tests (**406/406**), scope fixtures, and security gates passed. The CLI shard reported **3 failures across 2,493 completed segments** and timed out `compaction_continuity.test.ts`; one reported failure was `eval_dataset.test.ts`. The other failures were not fully recoverable from the shard output. The aggregate run exited **2**. It was not rerun after rebasing onto `cd755b3e`.

No independent review has been completed. Full-suite failure triage and qualification remain outstanding, so this is not a verified release result.

content.text: I found the cause: this checkout gives the trusted compiler-scan helper group-write permissions, and the evaluator deliberately refuses to qualify when that security prerequisite is violated. ## Status: IMPLEMENTED_QUALIFICATION_PENDING

The context maturity implementation is on `release/v1.3.0` work branch `codex/context-maturity-v130`. It is **not pushed or merged**. Claude owns review and merge from here.

### Branch and worktree

- The initial implementation worktree was based on `release/v1.3.0`; it was rebased without conflicts onto release commit `f4333a359b142e7440a75932506a36d7dbabb924`.
- Final commit: `6f2a91f317193d5ee00ae34688f6c999d8fc3055`.
- The worktree is 32 commits ahead of `origin/release/v1.3.0`. The unrelated untracked `cli/.local/` files remain untouched.
- The owner checkout was not modified. I released the completed suite and documentation claims.

### Implementation and assessment

The implementation adds inspectable context inventories and per-request manifests, bounded collection with source timing and explicit partial/failure outcomes, freshness labels and repository-change invalidation, source references through session persistence, compaction, resume and export, and operator-controlled durable memory with provenance and retention metadata. Model-originated memory promotion remains denied.

The four dimensions remain independently rated; there is no combined score:

- **Navigability:** 2 — Exploratory
- **Retrieval speed:** 2 — Exploratory
- **Freshness:** 1 — Ad hoc
- **Compounding value:** 1 in the no-memory fixture; 2 — Exploratory when carried durable notes or compaction links are evidenced

The baseline, design decisions, limitations and qualification record are in [CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md](/home/mike/nexus-wt/context-maturity-v130/docs/research/context-engineering/CONTEXT-MATURITY-SYSTEM.md).

### Verification

- `make build` passed on the rebased source.
- Focused context, memory, provider-wire, routing and session/export checks passed **158/158**.
- `make test` passed on a detached snapshot of exact source head `eda532061b8f78c67ddc3ffe4e3c3621312fd4eb`: Rust core **53/53**, TUI **406/406**, CLI shards **3,165/3,169** and **2,956/2,969**, both with zero failures, scope fixtures passed, and lifecycle security gates passed. The CLI shard skips were 4 and 13, respectively.
- Provider wire matrix passed **90/90** across local adapter fixtures. No inference provider or homelab-ai change was required.

### Remaining qualification gaps

Freshness for individual memory sources remains unknown; retrieval SLOs and held-out memory quality are unmeasured. Client-side manifests do not prove provider receipt. Independent review, hosted checks, and installed acceptance are still pending, so this is not a release qualification claim.

- This goal persists across turns. Ending this turn does not require shrinking the objective to what fits now.
- Keep the full objective intact. If it cannot be finished now, make concrete progress toward the real requested end state, leave the goal active, and do not redefine success around a smaller or easier task.

Work from evidence:
Use the current worktree and external state as authoritative. Previous conversation context can help locate relevant work, but inspect the current state before relying on it. Improve, replace, or remove existing work as needed to satisfy the actual objective.

No-progress check:
- Classify the previous goal turn as progress, a verified wait, or no progress. Progress changes authoritative state, completes work, or yields evidence that changes the next action; status restatements and unexecuted plans are no progress.
- A verified wait polls a specific process, session, job, or tool handle confirmed live now. Conversation, intent, prior output, or a lock or state file alone is insufficient. Treat work as stopped only when authoritative state says it is terminal or its handle is missing. An observation timeout or transient polling failure is not terminal: re-poll the same handle or inspect other authoritative state; never restart solely because observation expired.
- Revalidate a no-progress turn and take the next available safe action. If none exists because the same genuine blocker remains, report it and leave the goal active until the blocked audit threshold is met. Treat equivalent blockers as the same condition across turns even when their wording or stated next step changes.

Fidelity:
- Optimize each turn for movement toward the requested end state, not for the smallest stable-looking subset or easiest passing change.
- Do not substitute a narrower, safer, smaller, merely compatible, or easier-to-test solution because it is more likely to pass current tests.
- Treat alignment as movement toward the requested end state. An edit is aligned only if it makes the requested final state more true; useful-looking behavior that preserves a different end state is misaligned.

Completion audit:
Before deciding that the goal is achieved, treat completion as unproven and verify it against the actual current state:
- Derive concrete requirements from the objective and any referenced files, plans, specifications, issues, or user instructions.
- Preserve the original scope; do not redefine success around the work that already exists.
- For every explicit requirement, numbered item, named artifact, command, test, gate, invariant, and deliverable, identify the authoritative evidence that would prove it, then inspect the relevant current-state sources: files, command output, test results, PR state, rendered artifacts, runtime behavior, or other authoritative evidence.
- For each item, determine whether the evidence proves completion, contradicts completion, shows incomplete work, is too weak or indirect to verify completion, or is missing.
- Match the verification scope to the requirement's scope; do not use a narrow check to support a broad claim.
- Treat tests, manifests, verifiers, green checks, and search results as evidence only after confirming they cover the relevant requirement.
- Treat uncertain or indirect evidence as not achieved; gather stronger evidence or continue the work.
- The audit must prove completion, not merely fail to find obvious remaining work.

Do not rely on intent, partial progress, memory of earlier work, or a plausible final answer as proof of completion. Marking the goal complete is a claim that the full objective has been finished and can withstand requirement-by-requirement scrutiny. Only mark the goal achieved when current evidence proves every requirement has been satisfied and no required work remains. If the evidence is incomplete, weak, indirect, merely consistent with completion, or leaves any requirement missing, incomplete, or unverified, keep working instead of marking the goal complete. If the objective is achieved, call update_goal with status "complete" so usage accounting is preserved. If the achieved goal has a token budget, report the final consumed token budget to the user after update_goal succeeds.

Blocked audit:
- Do not call update_goal with status "blocked" the first time a blocker appears.
- Only use status "blocked" when the same blocking condition has repeated for at least three consecutive goal turns, counting the original/user-triggered turn and any automatic goal continuations.
- If the user resumes a goal that was previously marked "blocked", treat the resumed run as a fresh blocked audit. If the same blocking condition then repeats for at least three consecutive resumed goal turns, call update_goal with status "blocked" again.
- Use status "blocked" only when you are truly at an impasse and cannot make meaningful progress without user input or an external-state change.
- Once the blocked threshold is satisfied, do not keep reporting that you are still blocked while leaving the goal active; call update_goal with status "blocked".
- Never use status "blocked" merely because the work is hard, slow, uncertain, incomplete, or would benefit from clarification.

Call update_goal only after the completion or blocked audit passes, or when the user explicitly requests pausing this goal. For a requested pause, use status "paused", report the returned status, and stop goal work; never pause on your own initiative. Do not mark a goal complete merely because the budget is nearly exhausted or because you are stopping work.

</codex_internal_context>

I’ll continue from the release worktree and inspect the timed-out CLI tests to find a focused, reproducible issue. I’ll keep the broader context maturity requirements active; diagnosing the suite is just the next qualification step.
